Fixture: 32_icc_rgb_appl_32x32_lossless.jxl (+ 32_icc_rgb_appl_32x32_lossless.icc)
32x32 RGB, mathematically lossless, matrix-shaper ICC profile with the
"APPL" platform signature -- an E.4.3 byte-40 completion case

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 4 (18181-1 E.4.3). Identical to fixture 31 except that
header bytes 40..43 hold the primary platform signature "APPL" instead of
zeros.

E.4.3 predicts nothing for byte 40 and then completes bytes 41..43 from
whatever byte 40 decoded to: 'A' implies "PPL", 'M' implies "SFT". The
prediction is therefore self-referential -- it reads the output it has
already produced -- and a decoder that evaluated the ladder against the
*residuals* rather than the decoded header would get these three bytes
wrong and nothing else. Paired with fixture 33 ("MSFT") this pins both
completions.

Verification
------------
tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh checks two things on every run, and refuses to
write the fixture if either fails:

  * djxl --orig_icc_out returns a profile byte-identical to the one cjxl was
    given, so the reference really is what the codestream stores;
  * djxl decodes the pixels to a PNM byte-identical to the source, so the
    stream is mathematically lossless.

tests/e2e_icc.rs then asserts that JPXL's own E.4 decoder reproduces the
reference byte for byte, and repeats the comparison against a live djxl when
one is installed.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
